theme: C++ bridge, reward-hack adversaries, MAP-Elites gameplay truth, and action-feature preparation

questions.question: Can a C++ legal-action enumerator reproduce Python DecisionFrame action strings exactly across directed scenarios and fuzz traces?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the safest next step toward a C++ core engine without freezing bugs.

questions.question: What is the smallest compact C++ state representation that can replay Python fingerprints for common games?
questions.why_it_matters: Full Python object graphs are likely to bottleneck high-volume learning.

questions.question: Can any non-winning stall policy pass promotion under reasonable truncation rules?
questions.why_it_matters: A system that rewards stalling will poison every learning method.

questions.question: Which static MAP-Elites cells survive actual public gameplay evaluation across life totals and pilots?
questions.why_it_matters: Static construction priors are only candidate generators.

questions.question: Can a tiny action-ranker trained on public action features imitate code policies or heuristics better than raw slot baselines?
questions.why_it_matters: This is the lowest-risk neural-policy foothold.

questions.question: Can sequential racing eliminate bad constructor candidates with far fewer games than dense payoff tables?
questions.why_it_matters: Simulator throughput is limited; smarter allocation may matter more than faster kernels.

questions.question: Do policies or decks selected at 20 life transfer to 40 life, or does life total create separate empirical games?
questions.why_it_matters: Known-vs-unknown life construction remains a central dial.

questions.question: How much equity is available from learned mulligan/bottom decisions after construction is fixed?
questions.why_it_matters: Mulligans are an agent-facing decision surface, not just setup plumbing.

questions.question: Do Jace-lock, Overlord-clock, counter-wall, and stall-like profiles form intransitive cycles?
questions.why_it_matters: Mean win rate can hide metagame structure.

questions.question: When C++ kernels arrive, do payoff results remain unchanged under identical seeds and action indices?
questions.why_it_matters: Performance improvements must not silently change the game.
